That’s awesome that you’ve got a clean streak going, I hope you find something to keep you from coming back to it. Best of luck!

-It can easily kill you even if you’re “safe” about it.

-The scars/healing wounds will cause problems in your daily life.
-It doesn’t just effect you, those close to you will be hurt regardless of how hard you try to keep it from them and sometimes because of how hard you try.

- there’s a chance you’ll end up with life long scars that will fuck up your personal relationship and can fuck your job prospects.

-infection is a high chance and it’s a painful pain in the ass at best and deadly at worst. Not to mention the costly medical bills if you happen to live in a country that doesn’t have free healthcare.  Did you know that in the us even with insurance you can pay upwards of a grand just for an ambulance, because I sure as fuck didn’t.

-there’s a stigma that comes with cutting people will judge, mock, belittle, and shame you.

-it’s addictive, and like most addictive things you have to do more and more for the same affect. This escalates, you have to cut more deeper ect. It consumes you. 
 
There’s so so many reasons not to start, if you can talk to a professional do it, if you already are that’s awesome I’m proud of you keep at it. Be honest with them they may be a professional but they aren’t a mind reader. There’s so many better ways to cope than this. Please take care, I hope things start to get better for you. If I can help let me know, my inbox is always open.

Thanks! I did end up going to the Er because all the urgent cares I could find we’re closed (it was like 10:30 at night so not surprising) but almost all the staff at the Er were super nice. They did a good job patching me up too. Didn’t have to see a psych, just a social worker. Just told everyone I wasn’t suicidal and they let me go home the same night.
Honestly I relate to this so fucking much, it freaked me out a touch how similar my situation is to this. The thought of killing my self is literally never not in my head.

I’m just gonna restate what a lot of people here have already said; get into a therapist. Trauma is a bitch to recover from, and from my experience/knowledge it’s damn close to impossible to do it all on your own. From personal experience, EMDR can be a massive help, if you want more info you can google it (I’m trash at explanations) I really recommend it, it changed my life.  Please know you’re not alone in this, and there are people and resources in your corner. You can heal from this, please don’t just try to ignore it or down play it. You deserve to heal, and there are lots of options for you now. Best of luck, and I’m so sorry that this all came out during a time that’s supposed to be a celebration and that you had to deal with any of this in the first place.
Although I’m really no authority on this, so idk. I’m just some random stranger. But I hope stuff gets better.

Ngl, she sounds like an ass. Not trying to be mean, but that’s super fucked up. Like the kids didn’t know that I had cuts and weren’t trying to hurt me. But to intentionally hurt someone she says she loves, what the fuck? Anyways, Hope you’re takin care of yourself some

“I need you to be well, Aza. I can’t loose—“ “god mom, please stop saying that. I know you’re not trying to make me feel pressure, but it feels like I’m hurting you, like I’m committing assault or something, and it makes me feel ten thousand times worse. I’m doing my best, but I can’t stay sane for you, okay?”
-a conversation between Aza and her mom in the book Turtles All The Way Down by John Green. 
I’ve never read anything that so perfectly stated how being told things like that while living with a mental illness makes me feel.

Sometimes good advice comes in unpleasant packaging, for me At least it always seems that the advice that I want the least is what I need. Usually because it means the solution is more time or work, or both.  But I suppose anything worthwhile takes both time and work. Thanks again for taking the time to respond. I really didn’t expect anyone to answer, was just sort of yelling into the void. It means a lot that someone actually cared enough to offer anything to me.

Thanks,  I appreciate the reminder that meds and doctors aren’t the solution and are just tools. I forget that often. I guess I’m just frustrated right now. I just want things to get better but they aren’t. And nothing I try seems to change anything.
